releases.body:
# v0.49.26

This patch stops Magic Context from serving an old copy of text another OpenCode plugin adds to your messages. It also stops the historian from occasionally skipping or repeating a message on OpenCode 1.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Text another plugin adds on OpenCode 1:** some plugins add a text part to the current message on every step, for example a marker that changes from step to step. Magic Context treated that part as part of the conversation: it numbered it, saved its text, and on later steps put the saved copy back. The plugin's current text was replaced by an older one, which the plugin could then refuse.
  - **New parts:** text another plugin adds is now left exactly as that plugin wrote it. It's never numbered, saved or restored, and `ctx_reduce` skips its id.
  - **Existing sessions:** a part an older release already numbered keeps the bytes that release sent while the plugin's text is unchanged, so the upgrade doesn't break the prompt cache.

  OpenCode 2, Pi and Oh My Pi are unaffected.
- **Historian skipping or repeating a message on OpenCode 1:** Magic Context keeps a running count of each session's messages. OpenCode orders messages by when they were created, not when they were saved, so a message saved a few milliseconds late could be left out of that count until OpenCode restarted. The historian started each new chunk from the stored count, so it could skip one message for good, then summarize another twice after the restart. Now:
  - **Where the historian continues:** it starts after the last message it summarized, found by that message's id.
  - **Detecting a late save:** the count notices a message saved late and rebuilds itself. The check looks only at rows written since the last check, so it costs the same however long the session is.
  - **A wrong count found mid-run:** the run ends without publishing a summary and tries again once the count is rebuilt.

  Messages skipped before this release stay unsummarized. They are still in the session, and `ctx_expand` and `ctx_search` can read them.

# v0.49.25

This patch stops tool definitions from inflating Magic Context's token count and removes a whole-history copy from every turn of a Claude session with thinking on.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Tool definitions counted once for every tool ever seen:** on OpenCode, Magic Context added up every tool it had seen for a model and agent, across all sessions and projects, and never dropped one. After a restart this could make a session look full when it wasn't: a session at 76% could read as 98%, which triggered emergency cleanup and a cache rebuild. It also inflated the "Tool Defs" figure in the sidebar.
  - **OpenCode 2:** the count now uses exactly the tools the current request carries.
  - **OpenCode 1:** it counts the tools the model was offered recently. A tool stops counting once the model has been in use for about 10 minutes without it, and time spent idle doesn't count.

  Thanks to @jjjermiah.
- **Doctor on OpenCode 2:** the local embedding check now looks at the plugin copy OpenCode 2 actually loads.
- **Thinking sessions:** every turn of a Claude session with thinking on copied the whole message history in case a rare retry needed it. The copy is now taken only on turns where that retry can run. On large sessions this saves tens of milliseconds per turn. Thanks to @iceteaSA.

releases.name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.21
releases.body:
## Dashboard 0.20.21

Reads Broca logs that use one new log feature:

- `output-reservation/v1`: a record written before a step whose output cap Broca lowered so the request fits the model's window.

The dashboard doesn't use this record. Without this release, it stops reading a Broca log at the first record that requires the feature, and the steps after that point don't show.

releases.name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.20
releases.body:
## Dashboard 0.20.20

Reads Broca logs that use two new log features:

- `provider-fallback-block/v1`: a message can carry a part recording a provider's server-side switch to another model.
- `refusal-fallback/v1`: a refused model step is recorded, and a finished step can say which model actually served it.

The dashboard doesn't use these fields, and a run that carries them keeps all its steps and usage. Without this release, the dashboard stops reading a Broca log at the first record that requires one of these features.

# v0.49.24

This patch fixes several ways Oh My Pi could refuse every turn, keeps memory and note tool calls working on providers that drop optional arguments, and fixes two cases where the summarizer stopped summarizing.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.
- The `ctx_memory` and `ctx_note` tool definitions change in this release, so each open session rebuilds its prompt cache once, on its next turn.

## Fixed

- **Oh My Pi:** each of these left a session refusing every turn until a new session was started.
  - Resumed sessions were refused when Oh My Pi added a tool-control message to the request. Thanks to @tsankotsanev, who also sent the fix in #786.
  - Dropping a tool call could leave two assistant messages next to each other, and Oh My Pi's `Continue.` repair message wasn't expected. Thanks to @TheOrdinaryWow.
  - The first turn after a restart was refused when another session's background preparation was cancelled, including when several subagents started at once. Thanks to @Zireael.
  - A chained continuation was refused after a summary was folded into the history, because the history block's timestamps changed. Thanks to @Zireael.
  - A message typed while the agent was working was refused, because Oh My Pi's steering wrapper wasn't expected. Thanks to @Zireael.
  - After an aborted turn, every Claude turn was refused, because Oh My Pi drops an empty aborted reply that Magic Context still expected. Thanks to @TheOrdinaryWow.
- **`ctx_memory` and `ctx_note` on providers that drop optional arguments:** some providers, such as InferenceNet on OpenRouter, send only the first argument when a tool marks nothing as required, so almost every call failed. The key arguments are now required. Values that don't apply to an action can be sent empty, and when updating or merging a memory the model passes its current category to keep it. Thanks to @garionberg.
- **Summarizer:**
  - A session that runs from a single prompt is summarized again once it passes the execute threshold, instead of waiting for the 85% force band. Thanks to @yelrom-liively.
  - After an OpenCode session leaves Rust transform mode, the summarizer no longer refuses forever on gaps left by notification-only messages. Thanks to @iceteaSA.
- **Task permissions:** a task permission that denies everything and then allows named agents no longer hides the Task tool. Thanks to @selfagency for the report and @DreamchaserLG for the fix in #787.

## Changed

- When you answer a question that an Alfonso agent asked you, the summarizer now records your answer as your own words instead of dropping it with other system notices.
